ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are three circles in the figure, with centers labeled C, B, and A respectively. The three circles are arranged from left to right, circle C is the smallest, circle B is in the middle, and circle A is the largest. The three circles are externally tangent to each other in pairs, and the three centers are on the same horizontal line segment; the line segment goes from the center of C through the center of B and extends to the center of A, passing through the points of tangency of adjacent circles. Reasoning: The problem gives that the radius of circle A is 2 times that of circle B, and also 4 times that of circle C, so the radius ratio is r_A:r_B:r_C = 4:2:1. Let r_C = x, then r_B = 2x, r_A = 4x. The sum of the circumferences of the three circles is 42π, so 2π(x + 2x + 4x) = 42π, that is, 14πx = 42π, solving gives x = 3. Therefore r_C = 3, r_B = 6, r_A = 12. From the figure it can be known that AC is the distance from the center of circle C to the center of circle A, equal to CB plus BA. Because adjacent circles are externally tangent, CB = r_C + r_B, BA = r_B + r_A, so AC = (3 + 6) + (6 + 12) = 27.

method.method_draft: First read the image as three externally tangent circles whose centers C, B, and A lie on the same horizontal line, with segment AC passing through the tangency points. From the text, set the radii in the ratio r_A:r_B:r_C = 4:2:1. Let r_C = x, so r_B = 2x and r_A = 4x. The circumference sum gives 2π(x + 2x + 4x) = 42π, so x = 3. From the image, AC is the center-to-center distance from C to A, equal to (r_C + r_B) + (r_B + r_A) because adjacent circles are tangent. Thus AC = r_C + 2r_B + r_A = 3 + 12 + 12 = 27.

claims.claim: The circumference of a circle can be expressed as 2π multiplied by the radius.

claims.claim: From the three radius expressions and the sum of the circumferences, we get 2π(x + 2x + 4x) = 42π, solving gives x = 3.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: So 2π(x + 2x + 4x) = 42π, that is 14πx = 42π, solving gives x = 3
